assumptions: no split Berge cycle — the carrier hypothesis is still required; only the LANGUAGE hypothesis is dropped
attrs.evidence: This is Yannakakis' 1981 semijoin full reducer / Bernstein–Chiu 1981, and Dechter–Pearl 1989 tree clustering, specialised to singleton separators. Implemented and checked against brute-force satisfiability on every no-split federation of the round-1 space for four languages — OR/NAND, pins-plus-≠, <-and-=, and eq/neq as a control — with zero disagreements, including 6,960 federations that are locally satisfiable and globally unsatisfiable and therefore lie outside any language-wide theorem. This is the operationally important route for cell 36: where a value sort cannot have a transitive core, this still decides.

keyed_entries.value: the block-cut tree of the union carrier, under no split Berge cycle

attrs.prior_art: Yannakakis, Algorithms for Acyclic Database Schemes, VLDB 1981 · Dechter & Pearl, Tree Clustering for Constraint Networks, AI 38 (1989). KNOWN, not re-derived; what is claimed here is that it runs and agrees.
attrs.statement: Under no split Berge cycle, one leaf-to-root pass of exact unary separator projections over the super-block tree decides union satisfiability, with NO hypothesis on the constraint language.
